function: p. 3: Deep-unfolded projected-gradient precoder (DUBM) with learned step-sizes computes leakage-based (SLNR) transmit precoders for user-centric cell-free massive MIMO under per-AP power constraints.
system: p. 1: Cell-free massive MIMO downlink: Q APs with M antennas, I single-antenna UEs, clustered APs; simulated Q=24, M=4, I=6 (p. 4); band not stated; no RIS.
method: p. 3: Deep unfolding of IOM: L=2 layers of K=4 projected-gradient steps, LK=8 learnable step-sizes, trained unsupervised with negative leakage sum-rate loss (Adam, mini-batch 10, p. 4).
data_channel: p. 4: Custom simulator: complex Gaussian (Rayleigh) small-scale fading, path loss C0=-30 dB at 1 m with exponent 3, AP-UE distances random in [60, 320] m; training data self-generated.
test_conditions: p. 4: Trained on Q=4 APs, M=4, I=6, distances 100-200 m, all APs serving each UE; tested with Q=24 APs, distances 60-320 m, overlapped and non-overlapped AP clusters.
baselines: p. 4: WMMSE and modified RWMMSE (non-learned), DUWMMSE (deep-unfolded WMMSE, learned); the paper's own IOM is also compared.
metrics: p. 4: Leakage sum-rate and sum-rate versus iteration (Figs. 3, 5), training loss (Fig. 4), running time per iteration (Fig. 6, p. 5), number of trained parameters.
complexity: p. 4: IOM precoder update O(KIQbar M^3 log2 eps + KIQbar^2 M^2), DUBM O(KIQbar^2 M^2); LK=8 trained parameters; running time in Fig. 6 (p. 5).
q1_support: p. 4: "The path loss is modeled as" - custom simulator with CN(0, I) small-scale fading and a distance-based path loss; no 3GPP model, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 5: "can be directly used in the scenario with a different number of APs" - step-sizes learned with Q = 4 APs (p. 4) are applied with Q = 24 APs, another distance range and other AP clustering.
q3_support: p. 5: "the WMMSE and DUWMMSE methods, respectively" - IOM and DUBM reach slightly higher sum-rate than classical WMMSE and than the learned deep-unfolded WMMSE (Fig. 5, p. 4); RWMMSE is also compared.
q4_support: p. 4: "In contrast, the computational complexity in obtaining" - DUBM precoder update O(K I Qbar^2 M^2) versus IOM O(K I Qbar M^3 log2 eps + K I Qbar^2 M^2); p. 5: "The running time of the WMMSE, IOM, DUWMMSE, DUBM and" compares measured runtimes (Fig. 6).
q5_support: p. 4: "The training dataset is generated in the" - scenario with Q = 4, M = 4, I = 6 from the paper's own simulator; no code or data link and no public or measured dataset.
notes: Included, area 3: DUBM is deep unfolding with LK = 8 trained step-sizes, so it counts as learned although the other proposed method, IOM, is classical optimization. q2: step-sizes trained with Q = 4 are applied with Q = 24 (pp. 4-5). Unsupervised is my label, since the loss is the negative leakage sum-rate without labels. The paper does not say how DUWMMSE is trained; it is described as the deep-unfolded WMMSE of refs [6]-[8]. Perfect CSI is assumed at the APs (p. 2).
